question: Which pathways does PTEN participate in?

model.site: other: You are an input classifier for a biomedical evidence search

model.reply:
PTEN is a phosphatidylinositol-3,4,5-trisphosphate 3-phosphatase that negatively regulates the AKT/PKB signaling pathway by dephosphorylating phosphoinositide substrates, functioning as a tumor suppressor [10: "negatively regulates intracellular levels of phosphatidylinositol-3,4,5-trisphosphate in cells and functions as a tumor suppressor by negatively regulating AKT/PKB signaling pathway"][10: "preferentially dephosphorylates phosphoinositide substrates"]. It directly opposes the oncogenic PI3K/AKT/mTOR signalling network by metabolising PIP3 [25: "PTEN is a phosphatase which metabolises PIP3, the lipid product of PI 3-Kinase, directly opposing the activation of the oncogenic PI3K/AKT/mTOR signalling network"].

## PI3K/AKT/mTOR Signalling

PTEN loss of function represents one of the most common events observed across many cancer types, with the most frequent mechanisms being single-copy gene deletion and epigenetic silencing rather than coding-sequence mutations [25: "loss of function of the PTEN tumour suppressor is one of the most common events observed in many types of cancer"][25: "the most frequently observed events are deletion of a single gene copy of PTEN and gene silencing"]. In the cytoplasm, PTEN tumor suppressor opposes the PI3K/Akt signaling pathway [26: "PTEN tumor suppressor opposes the PI3K/Akt signaling pathway in the cytoplasm"].

## Nuclear Functions and Chromosomal Integrity

PTEN maintains chromosomal integrity in the nucleus, and its nucleus-cytoplasm shuttling is regulated by ubiquitylation, SUMOylation, and phosphorylation [26: "maintains chromosomal integrity in the nucleus"][26: "Nucleus-cytoplasm shuttling of PTEN is regulated by ubiquitylation, SUMOylation and phosphorylation"]. Under high glucose conditions, PTEN is conjugated by Nedd8, which induces its nuclear import; neddylated PTEN promotes cell proliferation and de novo fatty acid synthesis, correlating with tumor progression and poor prognosis in breast cancer [26: "PTEN is conjugated by Nedd8 under high glucose conditions, which induces PTEN nuclear import"][26: "neddylated PTEN correlates with tumor progression and poor prognosis"].

## Immune Regulation via cGAS-STING

PTEN loss suppresses cGAS-STING pathway activity in glioblastoma, with mutant PTEN patients showing decreased STING, IRF3, NF-KB1, and RELA mRNA expression alongside reduced CD8 infiltration and Granzyme B levels [28: "Decreased STING, IRF3, NF-KB1, and RELA mRNA expressions were also found in patients with mutant PTEN"][28: "CD8 infiltration, cGAMP, and Granzyme B levels were reduced in the PTEN loss group"]. Determining PTEN status in glioblastoma tumours is important when considering immunotherapeutic agents [28: "determining the PTEN status in tumours is of great importance, like in situations when considering the treatment of glioblastoma patients with immunotherapeutic agents"].

## Secreted PTEN and Antitumor Immunity

PTEN can be secreted through a TMED10-channeled protein secretion pathway and binds to PLXDC2 on macrophages, activating JAK2-STAT1 signaling that switches tumor-associated macrophages from an immunosuppressive to inflammatory phenotype [29: "extracellular PTEN binds to the plexin domain-containing protein 2 (PLXDC2) on macrophages, triggering subsequent activation of JAK2-STAT1 signaling"][29: "switches tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) from the immunosuppressive to inflammatory phenotype"]. Intratumoral injection of PTEN protein promotes antitumor immunity and enhances the therapeutic efficacy of anti-PD-1 treatment in mice [29: "intratumoral injection of PTEN protein promotes antitumor immunity and suppresses tumor growth in mice"][29: "PTEN treatment also enhances the therapeutic efficacy of anti-PD-1 treatment in mice"].

PTEN participates in several interconnected pathways: it negatively regulates the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signalling network by metabolising PIP3 [10], maintains chromosomal integrity in the nucleus [26], modulates the cGAS-STING inflammatory pathway [28], and drives antitumor immunity through JAK2-STAT1 signalling in macrophages [29].

## Core Signalling Pathway

PTEN functions as a phosphatidylinositol-3,4,5-trisphosphate 3-phosphatase that preferentially dephosphorylates phosphoinositide substrates, directly opposing the activation of the oncogenic PI3K/AKT/mTOR signalling network [10][25]. The gene PTEN, formally designated PHOSPHATASE AND TENSIN HOMOLOG; PTEN, was identified as a tumor suppressor mutated at high frequency across many cancer types [4][10].

## Nuclear Functions and Neddylation

PTEN shuttles between the nucleus and cytoplasm, where nuclear PTEN maintains chromosomal integrity and exhibits tumor-suppressive functions [26]. Under high glucose conditions, PTEN is conjugated by Nedd8, which induces its nuclear import; neddylated PTEN then promotes cell proliferation and de novo fatty acid synthesis rather than suppressing it, correlating with tumor progression and poor prognosis in breast cancer [26].

## Immune Regulation Pathways

PTEN loss is linked to immunosuppression through the cGAS-STING pathway in glioblastoma, where mutant PTEN patients show decreased STING, IRF3, and NF-KB1 expression along with reduced CD8 infiltration and Granzyme B levels [28]. Secreted PTEN binds PLXDC2 on macrophages, activating JAK2-STAT1 signalling that switches tumor-associated macrophages from an immunosuppressive to inflammatory phenotype and enhances anti-PD-1 therapeutic efficacy [29].

## Clinical Contexts and Variants

Several clinical trials target PTEN-related pathways, including Sirolimus to Treat Cowden Syndrome and Other PTEN Hamartomatous Tumor Syndromes [11] and Akt Inhibitor MK2206 in Treating Patients With Advanced Breast Cancer [23]. Additional trials examine PTEN and IGFBP-3 Correlation in Ovarian Carcinoma Invasion [6], PTEN Protein and mRNA in Malignant Cells of Chronic Myelomonocytic Leukemia [15], and Can Dormant Perimenopausal Ovarian Follicles Become FSH Responsive? [19]. ClinVar records multiple PTEN variants including NM_000314.8(PTEN):c.-193C>G [3], NM_000314.8(PTEN):c.165-4T>A [9], NM_000314.8(PTEN):c.-515G>C [14], NM_000314.8(PTEN):c.-248C>T [18], and NM_000314.8(PTEN):c.224A>C (p.His75Pro) [22]. Associated publications include PMID 30738865 [7], PMID 33299139 [12], PMID 37547448 [16], PMID 38214828 [20], and PMID 39197453 [24]. In triple-negative breast carcinoma, PTEN protein expression and copy number variation were assessed in pretreatment and posttreatment specimens [13][27], and mechanisms of PTEN loss in cancer were reviewed across seven common tumour types [2]. PTEN expression in TNBC showed discordance between pretreatment and posttreatment primary tumors in 5% of patients and between posttreatment primary tumors and lymph node metastases in 9% [27].
